# GraphScene's e2e reads its labels before the resized frame draws

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/rendering/GraphScene.spec.mjs:117` failed on hosted `dev` push run [42285892908](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42285892908) at `5f57baeadf`, e2e-engine shard 7. A rerun of the shard passed.

```text
expect(drawn.labels.drawn.length, 'the frame places some of them').toBeGreaterThan(0)
Received: 0
```

The trace records the test's only stats read:

| read | frames | canvas | labels.count | uploaded.labels | labels.drawn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | `[2000, 1288]` | 20 | 20 | 0 |

The buffer already had the CSS size times 2, but only one frame had drawn.

## The Problem

Every test in this spec starts from `sizedSceneDrawn`. It waits for `frames > 0`, the demo's node count, and `canvas` equal to the CSS size times the ratio, and its JSDoc says that means "the demo scene drawn into a buffer of the canvas's CSS size". That doesn't hold.

`GraphScene#updateSize` resizes the buffer synchronously and only requests the frame. A read that lands between the size message and the next animation slot sees the new buffer beside the previous frame's drawing. Here the previous frame was the boot frame, drawn before any size message, and it placed no labels. On a fast runner the slot fires before the read; on a contended one it does not.

#19444 (PR #19445) moved these tests onto the sized buffer for this same boot race. The size is set before the frame that uses it, though, so the race survived. The labels assertions added by #20286 are the first to depend on what is drawn at that size.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/canvas/GraphScene.mjs:1404` `updateSize()` sets `canvasSize`, the buffer and the viewport at once, and owes the frame through `requestFrame()` (`:1339`).
- `requestFrame()` holds `animationId` until `render()` (`:1262`) clears it as it starts. `render()` places the labels (`drawLabels`) and counts `frames`.
- `getStats()` (`:935`) reads `canvas` from the live buffer, and `frames` and `labels.drawn` from the last frame. Nothing in it says whether a frame is owed.
- `examples/component/graphScene/MainContainer.mjs:148` spreads `getStats()` onto the stats line the spec reads. The first test's "boot frames settle" loop (two reads agreeing on `frames`) waits out late boot frames, whether owed or still in transit.

## The Fix

1. `GraphScene#getStats()` reports `owed`: a frame was requested and has not drawn yet. Until it draws, `frames` and `labels.drawn` describe the last frame, not the current state. The engine already tracks this in `animationId`, so the change exposes it and adds no bookkeeping.
2. `sizedSceneDrawn` also waits for `!owed`, so the read it returns is of a frame drawn at the sized buffer.
3. The first test's settle loop stays. Deleting it failed 1 of 3 local runs: after the read with no frame owed (`frames 2`), a third frame landed in the idle second with the buffer, camera and labels unchanged. Boot can still reach the renderer after its first sized frame, and `owed` cannot see a message that is still in transit.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.canvas.GraphScene#getStats().owed` | `animationId`, set by `requestFrame()` and cleared by `render()` | `true` from a frame request until that frame starts | a paused scene or a lost context owes nothing, since `requestFrame()` requests nothing | `getStats` JSDoc | a unit arm: `true` after a request, `false` once the frame runs |

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `getStats().owed` is `true` after `requestFrame()` and `false` once the owed frame runs, asserted in `test/playwright/unit/canvas/GraphScene.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] `sizedSceneDrawn` waits for `!owed`, and its JSDoc says what the returned read shows.
- [ ] ~~The first test's "boot frames settle" loop is gone.~~ Withdrawn 2026-11-06 (The Fix, item 3): the loop also waits out boot messages still in transit, which `owed` cannot see. Its comment now says so.
- [ ] The e2e spec passes locally through the off-socket engine tier with `--repeat-each=3`.

## Out of Scope

- Whether the boot frame should place labels before the first size message. That is a one-frame state in the default 300×150 buffer.
- Other GraphScene CI notes with a different shape.

## Avoided Traps

- **Waiting for `frames` to advance once the size matches.** When the size message lands before the boot frame's slot, that frame already draws at the size and no other frame is owed, so the wait would hang.
- **Waiting for `labels.drawn.length > 0` in the helper.** The "places some of them" assertion would become its own precondition, and a scene that never draws labels would fail as a timeout with the wrong message.
- **Two reads that agree on `frames`.** Both can land before the slot on a contended runner. That narrows the race but never closes it.
